steps.text: I see it.
I see Alfonso heading to the great hall every day. He's named it 'Iberia.'
He's moved the mirror from his bedroom to the hall, and spends day after day examining himself.
Ever since the head chef and young Jamie were executed, he and I are the only ones left.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: There you are.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: How long was I asleep? Feels like I barely got any rest before I found myself awake.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Uhh... Not long... But...

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: No need to force yourself. I know it hurts when you talk.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: These lowly monsters leave plenty of blood behind, so let's use that to write instead.
I nod. In the corner are buckets, filled with the blood of our quarry.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Time passes too slowly. I barely slept at all, but my dreams felt even longer than all the decades behind us...

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Is it time we gave up then? It's been a long, long while since young Jamie and the old chef left us. Should we follow them?
We should give up.
My consciousness blurs more and more, like the feeling of being entangled right before waking from a dream.
It is not just my flesh that is changing, but everything about me. Everything that makes me a living being.
We should give up. We should end ourselves before we're devoured. The infinite, boundless ocean. The sea breeze. The waves. The whispers.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Chief Mate, this is our ship. Our ideals.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Sooner or later, we'll lose even the strength to walk. But that won't happen to her. Not the Stultifera Navis.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: That cigar-chomping engineer was right. Even if we all die, this ship will never sink.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Today... is just another twenty-four hours in one long, unending day.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: ... (Scrawls some words using the blood of Sea Terrors)

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Don't... give up?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Hah! Look at what you've become. I can't even see your sea-blue eyes anymore. Wouldn't you rather be set free?

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Scrawls) I am your chief mate.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: For... your sake...

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Hush, easy now.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Thank you, Garcia. No matter what you turn into, the bond between us will never change.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Nods)
But I know. He is looking at the mirror. Because even someone as strong as him... has finally succumbed to the monsters.
We have consumed their flesh and blood. At first, we started fires to cook them. Then, we were forced to devour them raw.
Even the most powerful Inquisitors were awed by Alfonso's strength. He was the object of so many young sailors' admiration. There was nothing he couldn't do.
But he has held on long enough. Soon, he too will become one of the monsters.
He is worried. He is furious.
If he cannot even tolerate the slightest monster within him, how can he tolerate me?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Trash. You're worth even less than the weed that washed ashore in Sal Viento. That woman was merely creating a smokescreen.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The ocean boasts no changes to speak of.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...I want to see. Are you free?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Friends are here. They are trapped. Need help. Should be returned to our kin's embrace.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Many friends have died here. But Parents. Will not let them die. I must save them.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Even if you can speak with that ugly mug of yours, that's no surprise to anyone.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Return to the great sea. No need to fight.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: We go, together—

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: I've already grown tired of your prattling. Time to end you.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...Gla-dia, will you prey on me?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: If you feed on me, will that make you stronger? More full of life?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Will it help the scales on your neck grow and spread, and return you to your proper form?

a.text: Abyssal Hunters are bound by blood.
The Seaborn contorts its relatively slender form. It is—
—biting off parts of its own body.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: I sever... this flesh. Consume it.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: If you need more, I give you more. I will give you everything.
Gladiia stares blankly at the fleshy mass on the ground.
She is shaken.
But not because of the Seaborn, or its behavior.
However, this moment of distraction convinces the Seaborn that Gladiia has accepted its proposal.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...We will meet again soon.
The Seaborn leaves, the Gladiia does not pursue it.
Because she smells the scents of Shark and Skadi. The Seaborn will not escape.
She turns around, and heads towards where another smell is coming from.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The smell of the sea... and of blood. The smell of Hunters. Aboard the ship? And I didn't notice it until I got this close?

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Impossible!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What... What do we do now?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Never expected there'd be people alive here. I thought we'd get the ship back just by killing some Sea Terrors. The Captain made it sound so simple.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: What are you looking at, Specter?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: The mirror.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Did you know, Skadi? Even as we speak, when I look at myself in this mirror, I start to remember so many things that I'd forgotten.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: A darkened dome. A hundred-meter tall sculpture. An aquamarine-colored opera hall. A waterfall pouring crystals of ice. What is this place, Skadi?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: ...Your home.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: My home... I remember now.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Writhing flesh climbing all over that statue. It collapses with a thunderous thud.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I remember these things, but... But I've never experienced them.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Dunno. I only know it from hearing you talk about where you used to live, which fell into ruin long ago. Long before I met you.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Maybe you only saw the report later on.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Can we save the chatter for some other time?!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Were we planning to chase down those two Seaborn, or are we seizing control of the ship while they're not around and, uh, sailing it back?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: If the survivors haven't managed it in sixty years, somehow I doubt we could figure it out ourselves.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Just be patient. The squad leader will figure something out... Ugh.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Specter! What's wrong?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Just... a little dizzy.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I just remembered... what they did to me. I...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: I saw her just now in Gran Faro...?

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: She was willing to talk to me. She was full of hypocrisy, blowing hot and cold, but she...

steps.name: Specter
steps.text: She's here.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What... You mean more survivors?

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: No, an enemy. One who can cross the sea and board this vessel, which is more than enough to identify them.

steps.name: Skadi
steps.text: Let's split up. Where will you go?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I am an Iberian Inquisitor. It is my duty to ensure that this ship returns to Iberia's hands.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: I'll go after that— after Alfonso!

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Slithers away hastily)

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Gahh—!

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Oh, don't you worry, Garcia. We'll catch up soon enough.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: When those ignorant Ægirs wounded it, it went up through Victoria, and past Bolívar. From there, it could only climb up onto the deck, then dive into the sea.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: This ship is not at its beck and call.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Leithanien. When we were young, we visited that country along with some other officers. Do you still remember?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: The twisted faces of those Kurfürsten were enough to turn stomachs. But they understood how to respect Arts, which was a mind-boggling revelation...

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Hmm...?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Today's been a good day. We saw quite a few living people. Hope they get out quickly though.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Go. Go to 'Leithanien,' Garcia. Go play the scores you used to love so much.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Breathe some life into the hunt, my love.

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Nods)

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Hrgh—!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You, are not scaleless. Do you need food?

steps.name: Sea Terror
steps.text: (Encircling slithering sounds)

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Sufficient nutrition. But these waters, are still incomplete. The Cycle has not yet been built, and living things die in vain.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: We must hurry—

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: —Why? Hunting, meaningless. There is something we must do, a duty to our kin.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: How many does that make now? Lost track after ten. When'd you monsters learn how to talk?

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Ohh... No, I remember you, little one. When we ate your parents, you and your litter were nearby, watching.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Back then, you were the weakest of the lot. Pathetic runt.
Alfonso laughs as he pokes at the Seaborn's wound, blood running along the tip of his blade and dripping onto the floor.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: We are bound by blood. You hunt and eat us, you will become us. Just as our Parents hunted you, and then became hunted by you.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: If the right conditions can trigger your evolution, then how do we make you more palatable? Your flesh, that is.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: To hunt is to survive. There is no good or evil in the hunt.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: That's too bad then.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: The scent trail... ends here.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: He led me here. This smell...
Gladiia does not search for the Hunter's whereabouts.
She begins to look around her.
Ever since she boarded this vessel, her surroundings have filled her with a sense of nostalgia—the materials, the decorations, the handiwork.
Breogan, a genius from the Academy of Sciences, was an Ægir. Without a doubt, this was his domain.
The mystery behind why this ship hadn't sunk in decades was itself the message Breogan wanted to leave to the Ægir. A brand new fusion of Originium and terrestrial technologies.
But what exactly is it?
Gladiia grasps the key from her bosom.
She sizes up her surroundings.

steps.name: Gladiia
steps.text: Breogan... Where did you hide your secrets?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (Why would this ship be built like a palace?! Most of it is decorative, and there are even sculptures.)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (No, that's not all. Both the sculptures and the patterned carpets have been cleaned. Even under these conditions?)
(The sound of music wafts in from the distance)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: ...Someone's playing the piano?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: It's coming from over here!
Irene's footsteps slow down.
At the end of the corridor, through a crack in the door, she sees—
—A single Seaborn, slapping away at a dilapidated old piano.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (It's that Seaborn that was next to Alfonso! But what is it doing here?)

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Cheerfully slaps at the piano)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Ugh, what a ruckus... It's just pounding away at the keyboard with no rhyme or reason.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (Alfonso isn't here... Did he go after the Seaborn? Why is his chief mate here alone then?)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (Well, I won't worry about it for now.)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: —What?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (That melody just now, was that a coincidence? It certainly looks like it's only randomly smashing the keys.)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: (No... It stopped?)

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: ...The seashore... O, the seashore...

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Farewell to heroes... and... great men...

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: —! Hiss...!
The Chief Mate turns its head in fear. Fear. Fear is what Irene sees in its behavior.
A massive, inexplicable physical reaction. One that's never been displayed in front of a Hunter before.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Just now, you weren't just randomly hitting keys...?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: That... passage you played. An Iberian military song...? You... how?

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Urgh...!

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Y-You're still conscious? Do you still have memories of being human? Do you know who you are?

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But, no... You're already fully transformed. The Inquisition has dealt with cultists like that before. There's no reversing it.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Wh-What are you planning? What are you doing with your hand?!

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Carefully places its hand atop Irene's head)

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: What... What is the meaning of this?
Through the scraps of cloth reminiscent of a wedding veil, the Seaborn known as the chief mate watches Irene.
Its pupils are cloudy. It is suffering. It—
—is filled with both affection and nostalgia.

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: You... If you truly retain a shred of your humanity...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: But how, after all these years...?

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: Cap... tain...

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Wh-What's happening?!

steps.name: Inquisitor Irene
steps.text: Wait!

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Hunt, feed. But that is not what you are doing. Your goal is constantly changing. Shaking. Yes, shaking.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Tch.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: You should just keep playing your piano, Garcia. You don't need to be touching these—

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Lightly shakes head)

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Hah.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Then sink your teeth into it. Its body is changing. Finish it now.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: You are... not hungry.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Why?
Alfonso doesn't answer the Seaborn's question. He simply chops and hacks at it again and again, like meat on a cutting board.
The chief mate bites down on the Seaborn in a death grip. Its crown falls to the ground during the struggle, but it does not care to pick it up.
Alfonso cuts off the Seaborn's tentacles, which join the crown on the ground. The chief mate pauses for a moment.
Ah... Garcia, Garcia.
Look at your crown, and at that tentacle. Do you understand what you've become now?

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...Leave. We will meet again.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Garcia!
The chief mate lifts its head, but the Seaborn has already vanished without a trace.
It quietly picks up its crown, and places it back on its head before returning to Alfonso's side. As if apologizing, it gently rubs his hand.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...Are you hurt, my good chief mate? Or were you distracted by our uninvited guests?
The chief mate does not answer.
It dares not speak. It dares not say that when it was biting down into the enemy, it felt like it was 'tearing into its own kin.'
It dares not speak, and after once again realizing what it has become, it begins to feel guilt.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: ...If you still have room for emotions in your heart, then that is proof enough that you're still human. Remember young Jamie's last words? 'I have no remorse, no regrets, and no fear.'

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Only when you truly feel nothing will you lose the right to call yourself human.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: Don't worry. The next hunt will be quick, and as always, it WILL return.

steps.name: Captain Alfonso
steps.text: What's wrong?

steps.name: Chief Mate
steps.text: (Lightly shakes head)

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Herald.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: ...Kin. Scaleless?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You are badly wounded. A newborn like you should not have been in a hurry to board this ship.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Kin are here. In need of help.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Indeed, true enough. But you've been hurt. Though they are kin, they do not welcome you.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: They have not yet accepted their identity. They are still lost and confused.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Accept? Identity?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: ...You do not need to understand. These waters are still incomplete. Perhaps you will have to further perfect yourself before you can lead our entire kind.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: Need time. And nutrition.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: And I've come to give you both.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: That blasphemous sea captain slaughtered Sea Terrors for food, but used every means available to hinder the transformation. He's usurped pieces of the Cycle, yet refuses to be a part of it.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: The flesh and blood of those offspring rightfully belonged to you. Those nutrients were meant to be yours. This ship has delayed the birth of a brand new ecosystem.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Please do not abandon me, Herald. In due time, all of Terra will become one and the same with the Nest.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: I do not abandon. Kin.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: I need time. But not much more.

steps.name: Seaborn
steps.text: I will be back. We will meet again.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: I could have sworn you were going to rush over and kill us.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Should I be thanking you, Ulpianus?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I can kill something like whenever I want. It's even weaker than Quintus.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: How patient of you.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Gladiia also tried to infiltrate the Church of the Deep in Sal Viento, hoping to get something out of them. Of course, she was a poor fit, given her personality.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: And here I was thinking that none of you were a good fit. Or are you saying you're special?

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: You're getting less and less tight-lipped of late.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Heh. I suppose there's really no rhyme or reason for when you decide to keep quiet, Ulpianus.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Don't use my given name so casually, Liberi. You don't understand the weight behind it.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: We are enemies.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Oh, we both know you've already abandoned that notion, deep in your heart. Of course, you might still hold some 'enmity.'

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Like a lost and famished traveler who stumbles on a frozen, starving mangler-beast in the mountains.

steps.name: Amaia
steps.text: Did whatever Breogan left behind satisfy your imagination?

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: Far from it.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: The Seaborn have existed for even longer than the Ægir. For their history to be turned upside-down, there must be something behind it.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: If you care about the word of God, then so be it. The Seaborn are not gods, nor are their forefathers.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I have seen how your gods die, their screams coursing through the currents, their flesh and blood smeared across abyssal ravines. As the clan hovered overhead, I plunged into the unknown depths of Ægir's territory.

steps.name: Ulpianus
steps.text: I've seen it with my own eyes. Enough to shatter all the beliefs I'd held thus far. Afterwards, I will rebuild it. Ægir will be lifted up once more.
